description: Human-reviewed runtime and optional dependency versions for the Python 3.14 production lane. Package metadata in pyproject.toml governs compatible ranges; the complete transitive release lock governs the accepted Windows environment.

dependency_lane_policy.mcp: newest stable SDK minor line only; MCP 1.x stays a client wire-compatibility requirement, not a second server lane
dependency_lane_policy.runtime: at most two reviewed lanes per library where behavior changes across them (newest minor plus the oldest supported line)
dependency_lane_policy.development: newest available release, because newer tooling encodes newer and stricter rules; a new diagnostic is fixed or narrowly excepted, never suppressed by loosening a rule or threshold

licensed_result.note: The 0.7.6 licensed release gate is now fully green: 13 passed / 0 failed with returncode 0 in the declared dependency lane (mcp 2.2.0, mph 1.3.1, Python 3.14.6), with cleanup verified (collision_absent, lease_absent, process inventory complete and unchanged). Progression across the session was 5 passed / 8 failed, then 8/5, 12/1, and finally 13/0. The controlled engineering fixture was extended with the Floquet evidence and a real solve, and the remaining defects were closed on measurement: a study-step plist is a DoubleArray and cannot round-trip as a string, guarded solver_execution/destructive_session calls must declare expected_model_revision, model_load obeys the configured read roots, and a venv python.exe redirector breaks durable-job worker identity so the 0.7.6 environment is a full environment copy over the real interpreter. mph_lanes.policy: two reviewed lanes: the retained 1.3.1 reference lane and the 1.4.x line

notes: 0.7.6 moves the server SDK lane to the newest stable MCP Python SDK minor line and formally adopts MPh 1.4.0 alongside the retained 1.3.1 reference lane, per the recorded two-lane dependency policy.
SDK version, date-based protocol revision, and extension wire generation are separate identities; see comsol_mcp/protocol_identity.py. Upgrading the SDK does not implement the Tasks extension.
MCP 1.x client compatibility is preserved through the ordinary-tool wire path and is verified by legacy-protocol stdio tests, not by keeping a second SDK installed.
Python 3.14 remains the main development and production lane; Python 3.15 uses a separate experimental solver-free CI gate without semantic-docs or licensed acceptance.
The standard GIL-enabled CPython ABI is required; the free-threaded ABI is not accepted.
PyMuPDF is reviewed only for the manuals extra and is outside the default runtime release lock.
Optional semantic dependencies are outside the default runtime release lock.
